claims.finding: Five Form 4s were filed in the five weeks before the annual print (2026-07-30 twice, 2026-08-13, 2026-08-21, 2026-08-26), continuing a documented open-market buying programme by the two Elsztain brothers (Chairman and CEO) and director Saul Zang who together bought the equivalent of ~120,000 ADS at $10.57-$11.23 between 2026-04-22 and 2026-06-05, and there is not a single Form 144 in the whole 400-day index.

claims.why_not_priced: Form 4s from a foreign private issuer's controlling family are indexed but never aggregated - the corpus contains no news search at all for this ticker (n_queries=0 in every sweep) and the only place the April-June buys appear is one retail post. Three more filings land in the fortnight immediately before an annual results release, which is precisely the window when insiders normally cannot trade unless they have a standing plan or high conviction. If this were priced, the stock would not still be trading at roughly the same level as the chairman's May purchase price.

claims.finding: This is the fiscal-year-end release (year ended 30 June 2026) and at this company that is the release that carries the annual dividend proposal: the prior year distributed ARS 93,782m in cash plus IRSA shares, a stated ~8% yield, and the corpus records annual ADS distributions of $1.056 (2023) and $0.9921 (2024) with $0.50-1.00 expected this year against an $11.84 share price.
claims.why_not_priced: A dividend declaration that is 4-8% of market cap is a discrete cash event, and this issuer gets no US news coverage, no sell-side preview and no consensus in the whole capture. The size of the distribution is a function of ARS-denominated results that outside investors cannot model, so the announcement is a genuine information event rather than a formality.

claims.finding: The company's own reported numbers cut against the bull case the corpus repeats: adjusted EBITDA was 39.7% lower year on year in fiscal Q1 2026 and 19.0% lower in the fiscal first half, with agribusiness contributing only ARS 15,350m of ARS 137,967m, while the headline net income swing (ARS 193,932m against a prior-year loss) is attributed explicitly to 'the gain from changes in the fair value of IRSA investment properties' - a non-cash mark.
